messages:
alex: Heads-up: saw a 3x latency spike for small chat requests after a regional warm-pool drain this morning. Not full outage but cold-starts spiked tokens and cost.
jun: Which pool/region? any preemptible nodes involved?
alex: eu-west-1, mixture of dedicated + spot. The autoscaler drained ~40 nodes when CPU idle < 3% for 12m. We think we lost KV cache and attendant prefix caches.
michael: Ouch. Do we have logs correlating pod reschedules to node termination events? deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] autoscaler-event: NodePool eu-west-gpu-pool scaledDown count=42 reason=idleThreshold breach=12m
sara: We intentionally set aggressive downscale to save $$, but the user facing latency hit isn't acceptable. Idea: introduce a "rewarm handshake" — autoscaler marks nodes for 'pre-drain' with annotation and runtime can opt to keep KV cache alive or migrate.
jun: Sketch: autoscaler sets node annotation `infra.redwood/rewarm-intent=true` and emits event with TTL. Runtime agent on node sees it and either: 1) tags cached state to a shared cache (s3/redis) or 2) signals a grace period by touching the node lease. If no touch, proceed with cordon+drain.
alex: That would avoid immediate cache loss for short drains. We need safe default for spot nodes though (preemption can still happen without autoscaler warning).
michael: For preemptible VMs we can only do best-effort. But for Dedicated (non-preemptible) nodes this handshake could extend the drain window by configurable `rewarm_grace` (e.g., 3m) while cache snapshot completes.
sara: Also want metric-driven thresholds: not just CPU but model inference QPS and tail latency. If tail latency > target, raise min-keepalive for that pool.
jun: Implementation notes: change cluster-autoscaler scaler.go to emit NodeAnnotation and an event like:

```
annotations["infra.redwood/rewarm-request-ts"] = "2119876543"
```

and set condition on the node: `node.Spec.Taints += Taint{Key:"infra.redwood/rewarm", Effect:NoSchedule}` then runtime agent removes taint after snapshot.

(we should be careful — using taints for handshake might confuse other controllers)

michael: Alternative: use a CRD `RewarmRequest` referencing the node name. The runtime agent watches RewarmRequests.

sara: CRD is cleaner. avoids taint churn and race with other K8s controllers.

alex: Cost tradeoff: during rewarm we keep the node alive longer — need a budget. Proposal: add per-pool `rewarm_budget` (seconds) and `rewarm_cost_threshold` ($/hour) to nodepool config and enforce via autoscaler.
jun: We should add a metric exporter for `rewarm_seconds` and `rewarm_success` so we can quantify ROI.

oncall-bot: [oncall-bot] Paging: eu-west warmpool QPS spike tracked. Adding link to playbook: https://internal.redwood/playbooks/warm-rewarm

michael: Edge cases: 1) orphaned pods if node is preempted mid-snapshot; 2) KV snapshot size > network bandwidth causes long stalls — we should snapshot only hot keys and rely on shared prefix cache for rest.
sara: Suggest LRU-based selective snapshot: runtime records `hot_keys` per model and only persist top-N keys. Also compress snapshot (lz4) before upload.

alex: Another optimization: instead of full snapshot, publish a short 'warm-hint' describing active prefixes and last-token offsets. The next pod can pre-fetch only those prefixes to rebuild KV quickly.
jun: Also routing-layer aware: route new incoming requests to instances in other regions for the noisy burst instead of slow-rewarmed nodes. Add cross-region warmfail policy (fallback to regional replicated cache).
michael: Ops playbook adjustment: when drain > rewarm_budget, autoscaler should mark node as eviction-critical and proceed. Also alert when rewarm_success_rate < 70% for 24h.

sara: Implementation plan: (1) design CRD `RewarmRequest` + runtime agent watcher, (2) autoscaler emits request before cordon, (3) runtime responds with `RewarmStatus`, (4) metrics and dashboards, (5) rollout to dedicated pools then to spot with degraded guarantees.

alex: Can someone prototype a minimal CRD + agent this week? I'll wire up the dashboard once we have metrics.
jun: I can prototype the CRD and a small Go agent to watch requests and respond. Will push a draft PR to `infra/rewarm-crd`.
michael: I'll add autoscaler hook and tests. We should document API and failure modes in the playbook.

sara: Thanks — big win if we can avoid noisy cold starts without increasing baseline spend. :thumbsup:

alex: Great. tagging @oncall for visibility. I'll update the incident thread with status.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] PR created: infra/rewarm-crd #142 by jun
alex: Nice, closing thread for now. Follow-ups in PR.
